payload.headline: Apple holds at 355.58, still above every value estimate; no new business news

summary.thesis: Apple is a high-quality, cash-rich business, but the price of 355.58 assumes faster growth than it is showing, while forecasts are falling.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait for a breakout or a pullback that holds.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy from 300.56; swing entry only on a close above 361.9

payload.happening: Apple closed at 355.58, up 0.43%, in an uptrend and above its 50-day average of 342.84. The only news since the last note is a reported TechCrunch review of the iPhone Duo and a reported Black Friday streaming deals story, and neither affects the numbers. The next earnings report is due on 2027-01-28.
payload.business: The business itself is strong. Over the last twelve months, revenue was 478.8B, up from 416.2B, and free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 136.1B, up from 98.8B. Operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%. Two things are softening. Growth in the latest quarter slowed to 11.72%, down from 16.6% two quarters ago. And analysts have cut their forecasts: next-quarter earnings per share fell to 2.15 from 2.24, and next-year earnings fell to 10.6 from 10.84. The main risk to the business is inventory. It is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%, and unsold product can force price cuts that lower margins. The new investigation risk added to the annual report is a governance and sentiment issue for now, not a demand or margin issue. Cash is not at risk: liquidity is 56.7B, though debt of 80.1B exceeds cash of 36.3B, leaving net cash of -23.4B. Buybacks cut the share count by 1.56% over the year.

worth.text: At 355.58, Apple trades at 39.6 times its past earnings and 33.5 times next year's forecast earnings. It trades at 10.8 times sales, against a peer median of 5.3, which is the highest it has been in its own 5-year history. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 145.37 in the bear case, 202.38 in the base case and 265.87 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.1 to 300.56. What drives the gap is the assumed growth rate. To justify today's price, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 26.8% a year. At 20% starting growth the value is 273.62, and only at 30% does it reach 400.49. The margin assumption matters too: if operating margin fell to 24%, the value drops to 204.81.
worth.key_assumption: The price needs free cash flow to start growing at about 26.8% a year, well above last year's 15% sales growth.

bull: Free cash flow grew to 136.1B from 98.8B, which funds buybacks that cut the share count by 1.56% over the year.
Operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%, so the company is keeping more of each sale.
The price is in an uptrend, above a rising 50-day average of 342.84 and well above the 200-day average of 303.96.
bear: At 10.8 times sales against a peer median of 5.3, the stock trades at its highest level in its own 5-year history, which leaves little room for a miss.
Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%, which could lead to price cuts and lower margins.
Forecasts are falling: estimates are down 2.25% over 30 days, and quarterly growth slowed to 11.72% from 16.6%.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole value range of 145.37–300.56, so it is too high to buy.
The top of the value range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history, near the 200-day average of 303.96. Buying starts here.
The value if free cash flow starts growing at 20%, which is still faster than last year's 15% sales growth. Adding makes sense here.

longterm.why: The business is good, but the price assumes growth Apple is not showing, and forecasts are being cut. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: Resistance at 359.76–361.9 is less than one typical daily move away (the average true range, or ATR, is 8.56), and the macro read is negative. Enter only on a close above 361.9, or on a pullback that holds support at 347.89–351.46.

decision.timing: Options price a 5.1% move by 2026-12-18 and a 10.4% move by 2027-02-19, a window that covers the 2027-01-28 report. There is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.

change_mind: A drop to 300.56 (the top of the value range) would turn 'wait' into a long-term buy, and a drop to 273.62 would justify adding.

If the 2027-01-28 report shows operating margin holding at or above 33.01% and the next-year earnings estimate climbing back above 10.84, the inventory worry eases and the fair-value range would deserve a fresh look.
A daily close above 361.9 (the top of resistance) would turn the swing call from 'wait' to 'enter'.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because the only new items are two reported product and consumer stories, and the price of 355.58 is still above the top of the 145.37–300.56 value range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
